en.before: "Consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits" is the sentence to know. It converts programme design from good practice into a requirement with two named inputs.
en.after: Clause 9.2.2's two named inputs -- process importance and earlier audit results -- are the thing to know. It converts programme design from good practice into a requirement with two named inputs.

en.before: The purpose is stated too: so that audits focus on matters that are significant for the audit client and for achieving the audit programme objectives.
en.after: The purpose is stated too: so that audits stay focused on what matters to the audit client and on meeting the programme's objectives.

en.before: ISO 19011:2026 defines **audit criteria** as the set of requirements used as a reference against which objective evidence is compared. Its notes make the breadth explicit - criteria may include policies, procedures, work instructions, legal requirements, contractual obligations and industry standards.
en.after: ISO 19011:2026 defines **audit criteria** as the set of requirements used as a reference against which objective evidence is compared. Its notes make the breadth explicit - criteria may be policies, procedures or work instructions, legal requirements and contractual obligations and industry standards.

en.before: The comparison makes it unmistakable. **ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.2.2 a) requires the organization to define the audit *objectives*, criteria and scope for each audit.** Same harmonized structure, same clause number, one extra word. An auditor working across both standards who carries the 42001 wording into a 27001 audit will raise a finding the standard does not support.
en.after: The comparison makes it unmistakable. **ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.2.2 a) requires the organization to set the *objectives*, criteria and scope of each individual audit.** Same harmonized structure, same clause number, one extra word. An auditor working across both standards who carries the 42001 wording into a 27001 audit will raise a finding the standard does not support.

en.before: Do not confuse this with the exclusion that is not permitted. **ISO/IEC 27001 Clause 1 states that excluding any of the requirements specified in Clauses 4 to 10 is not acceptable when an organization claims conformity.** That governs the ISMS, not your audit.
en.after: Do not confuse this with the exclusion that is not permitted. **ISO/IEC 27001 Clause 1 states that leaving out any requirement of Clauses 4 to 10 is not acceptable where an organization claims conformity.** That governs the ISMS, not your audit.

en.before: Three notes follow. Remote methods can be combined with on-site methods to achieve a full and effective audit. They can be used for **virtual locations**. And they can be used by an auditor at one site of the auditee to audit another site.
en.after: Three notes follow. Remote methods can be mixed with on-site ones to make an audit full and effective. They can be used for **virtual locations**. And they can be used by an auditor at one of the auditee's sites to audit a different one.

en.before: Not annual. Not three-yearly. Not once per certification cycle. The standard leaves the interval to the organization, and it names what should inform it: the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits.
en.after: Not annual. Not three-yearly. Not once per certification cycle. The standard leaves the interval to the organization, and it names what should inform it: how important the audited processes are, and what earlier audits found.

en.before: The clause requires documented information as evidence of **the implementation of the audit programme and the audit results.** Two things, and organizations often have only the second.
en.after: The clause requires documented information showing **both that the programme was implemented and what the audits found.** Two things, and organizations often have only the second.
